correctness.rationale: Gaussian orthonormal bases are u_n=z^n/sqrt(n!) in L0 and v_n=z^n(n+1-|z|²)/sqrt((n+1)!) in L1, plus v_-1=conj(z). Angular orthogonality diagonalizes the interlevel disk operator. The coefficient equals the radial integral int_0^x t^n(n+1-t)e^(-t)dt/sqrt(n!(n+1)!) = e^(-x)x^(n+1)/sqrt(n!(n+1)!) by differentiation of t^(n+1)e^(-t). It is strictly positive, decays factorially, so gives the complete singular sequence and all S_p. Ratio a_(n+1)/a_n=x/sqrt((n+1)(n+2)) proves log-concavity and modal ties. Summing squares matches x e^(-2x) I1(2x). Maximizing each n at x=n+1 gives b_n increasing strictly to C=(2pi)^(-1/2), so for each finite x max_n a_n<C and limit norm is C. The Poisson representation a_n=sqrt(n+1)P(Pois(x)=n+1) with Stirling and entropy H(y)=y log y-y+1 gives Gaussian local profile and uniform tail control for every fixed p>0; Riemann sums establish the Schatten edge and level counting. Fixed-mode decay plus uniform norm proves strong limit zero despite norm nonconvergence. The verifier is finite corroboration, not the proof.
residual_risks: Claims depend on centered hard disk, Gaussian scale exactly pi^-1 exp(-|z|²), and the specified L1 normalization; p and threshold eta remain fixed.
The displayed inequality outside y in [1/2,2] uses a positive linear lower bound for H(y), which is valid away from its unique minimum at 1.
